images.title: One tray is one whole
images.purpose: Pose the question of how many whole units are in 8/3, 11/5 and 9/4, with the cue that one full tray of thirds, fifths or fourths is one whole.
images.composition: Three empty trays of exactly the same length stacked with wide gaps, each with its fraction to its right, and one question line below.
images.exact_structure: Three empty barfi trays, flat rectangles of exactly the same length and height, left aligned and stacked with wide gaps. Top tray: split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 3 equal cells, outlined teal #0072B2. Middle tray: exactly 5 equal cells, outlined amber #E69F00. Bottom tray: exactly 4 equal cells, outlined reddish purple #CC79A7. All cells empty; no barfi pieces drawn. Each tray's fraction sits to its right. Exactly 3 trays, 12 cells.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any barfi pieces drawn, any filled tray, or any count of whole units written
images.takeaway: Count how many full trays the numerator fills; the denominator is the tray size.
images.description: Three same-length empty trays cut into 3, 5 and 4 equal cells, next to 8/3, 11/5 and 9/4, with the cue that 1 full tray is 1 whole.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many pieces fill each tray, then how many full trays each fraction makes.

image_decisions.why: Empty trays sized by the denominator give the grouping cue for all three parts without filling any answer.
